newsitem.title: UK: BAA expects to pay 102 mln stg windfall tax.
newsitem.headline: BAA expects to pay 102 mln stg windfall tax.

text.p: British airports operator BAA Plc on Tuesday estimated it would have to pay 102 million pounds under the British government's new windfall tax on profits made by former state-owned utilities.
Previously the company had estimated its liability at between 70 and 100 million pounds after the new Labour government announced the proposed formula for assessing the tax on July 2.
But it said on Tuesday it was charging 102 million pounds as a provision for the tax on its first-quarter net profits, which were up 7.1 percent at 105 million pounds.
Pre-tax profits for the three months to June 30 rose 4.5 percent to 136 million pounds ($221.7 million) on turnover up 5.7 percent at 367 million pounds.

The company said first-quarter, pre-tax profits would have been up by 13.1 percent but growth was held back by the start in April of a new five-year price cap on its regulated charges at its London airports as well as accounting changes and the ending of differentials in peak and off-peak traffic charges.
Operating profits rose 5.7 percent, to 147 million pounds, boosted by a 7.8 percent rise in passenger traffic at its seven british airports over the period, to 26.5 million passengers.
BAA said traffic growth remained strong in July, despite the three-day cabin crew strike at British Airways Plc since many BA passengers were transferred to other carriers.
